title: Best Compressor Dehumidifier (2026): vs. Peltier & Desiccant
h1: The Best Compressor Dehumidifiers (and When Peltier or Desiccant Wins)
dek: Compressor units do the heavy lifting in most homes. Here are the ones worth buying, how they compare with Peltier and desiccant models, and what to do when the compressor quits.
description: The best compressor dehumidifier for every room, plus compressor vs. Peltier vs. desiccant explained and how to fix a compressor that runs hot or won’t start.
intro: Almost every dehumidifier that can keep up with a damp basement is a **compressor dehumidifier**. It works like a small air conditioner: a compressor pumps refrigerant through a cold coil, moisture in the air condenses on that coil and drips into a bucket, and the air is warmed back up on its way out. It’s the most efficient way to pull pints of water out of a warm, humid room.

That doesn’t make it the right choice everywhere. Tiny thermoelectric (Peltier) units are quieter and cheaper for a closet, and desiccant models keep working in cold garages where a compressor coil would ice over. Below are the compressor models we’d buy at each size, a plain-English comparison of the three technologies, and a troubleshooting guide for the most common compressor complaints.

blocks.text: That gap is the whole story. A compressor unit can remove dozens of times more water than a thermoelectric mini, which is why every basement pick on this page uses one. The trade-off comes as temperatures fall: below the 60s, a standard compressor’s coil starts to frost, and desiccants or low-temp models take over.

We don’t lab-test. We compared capacity under the 2019 DOE procedure, ENERGY STAR listings, manufacturer manuals (for humidistat type, drainage and operating temperature) and the CPSC recall database, then read owner reviews for patterns: compressors failing after a season or two, noisy cycling, leaky buckets and pumps that quit.
We chose one model for each common need — the best all-rounder, a pump model, a small unit, a budget pick and a cold-space specialist — rather than ranking five similar 50-pint boxes.

sections.heading: What to look for in a compressor dehumidifier

items.label: A current DOE 2019 rating
items.text: Older labels inflate capacity. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) translates old and new pint ratings.

items.label: ENERGY STAR certification
items.text: A compressor unit may run hundreds of hours a season. Certified models remove more water per kilowatt-hour, which adds up over a long season.

items.label: A set-percentage humidistat
items.text: It lets the compressor cycle off once the room reaches your target, saving energy and wear.

items.label: Auto-defrost and a low-temp rating
items.text: Essential for basements in the low 60s or below. Without it, the coil can ice up.

items.label: Drainage that matches the space
items.text: Gravity hose if there’s a floor drain, a built-in pump if water has to go up.

items.label: A meaningful warranty
items.text: The compressor is the most expensive part to fail. Some brands cover the sealed system longer than the rest of the unit — read the fine print.

blocks.text: For the right job, yes. A thermoelectric Peltier dehumidifier uses a solid-state module with one cold side and one hot side; air passes over the cold side and a little water condenses. There’s no compressor, so it’s quiet, light and inexpensive. But the Peltier effect is inefficient at moving heat, so these units remove only a small amount of water. They’re great for a closet, a small bathroom or a gun cabinet, and disappointing in a bedroom that’s genuinely damp. Our [small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) guide covers the best ones.

In a heated home in summer, a compressor wins on running cost. In an unheated garage, cabin or boat in the shoulder seasons, a desiccant keeps pulling water when a compressor would ice up. Our [desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/) guide goes deeper, and [how a dehumidifier works](/guides/how-does-a-dehumidifier-work/) explains the physics.

blocks.title: What’s the smallest compressor dehumidifier?
blocks.text: In the US, compact 20- to 22-pint units like the Midea Cube 20 are about as small as mainstream compressor dehumidifiers get. In the UK and Europe, 10- to 12-liter compressor models are common; see our [Meaco dehumidifier](/best/best-meaco-dehumidifier/) guide.

sections.heading: Dehumidifier compressor hot or not turning on? How to fix it

blocks.text: Most “dead compressor” calls turn out to be a setting, a safety delay or a dirty filter. Work through these steps before assuming the worst.

items: **Know that warm is normal.** A compressor dehumidifier releases heat, and the compressor housing and exhaust air are warm by design. Our [does a dehumidifier cool a room](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-cool-a-room/) explainer covers why.
**Wait a few minutes.** Most units hold the compressor off for about three minutes after power-up or a settings change to protect it.
**Check the humidistat.** If the room is already below your setpoint, only the fan runs. Lower the setting temporarily to test.
**Seat the bucket.** A full or misaligned bucket trips the float switch and stops the compressor.
**Look for defrost mode.** In a cool room, the compressor pauses while the fan melts frost off the coil. Frequent defrosting means the space is too cold for the unit.
**Clean the filter and coils.** Restricted airflow makes the compressor run hot and trip its overload protector, then restart a while later.
**Plug it straight into the wall.** Manufacturers advise against extension cords; low voltage can stop a compressor from starting.

**Listen for a hum or click.** A compressor that hums but won’t start, or clicks on and off every few seconds, often has a failed start component or a sealed-system problem. That’s a job for a technician or the warranty.

blocks.title: Can you fix a dehumidifier compressor yourself?
blocks.text: Not the sealed system. Refrigerant work requires EPA certification, and on a portable unit outside warranty, a new compressor usually costs more than the dehumidifier is worth. Our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide covers every other fix, and [how long dehumidifiers last](/guides/how-long-do-dehumidifiers-last/) helps you decide whether to repair or replace.

For most homes, the **Midea Cube 50** is the compressor dehumidifier to buy. Choose the **Frigidaire FFAP5033W1** if you need a pump, the **Midea Cube 20** for a single small room, the **Honeywell TP50AWKN** for a no-frills basement unit, and the **AlorAir Sentinel HD55** for a cold crawl space or basement. Save Peltier minis for closets and cabinets, and turn to a desiccant when the space drops toward freezing.

faqs.a: It’s a dehumidifier that uses a refrigerant compressor to chill a coil. Humid air condenses on the cold coil, the water drains to a bucket or hose, and the dried air is rewarmed and returned to the room. It’s the most common and efficient type for homes.

faqs.q: Is a compressor or desiccant dehumidifier better?
faqs.a: A compressor is better and cheaper to run in warm, humid spaces like summer basements and living areas. A desiccant is better in cold spaces — unheated garages, cabins and boats — because it doesn’t rely on a cold coil that can freeze.

Only for very small spaces. They’re quiet and inexpensive, but they remove a fraction of what a compressor unit does — often well under a pint a day. Use them in closets, small bathrooms and cabinets.

faqs.q: Is it normal for a dehumidifier compressor to be hot?
faqs.a: Warm, yes — compressors and the exhaust air run warm by design. If it’s too hot to touch and the unit keeps shutting off, clean the filter and coils and make sure air can circulate around it.

faqs.q: Why won’t my dehumidifier compressor turn on?
faqs.a: Common causes are the startup delay, a humidistat set above the room’s humidity, a full or misaligned bucket, defrost mode in a cold room, or an extension cord. If it hums or clicks without starting, call a technician or use the warranty.

faqs.q: Do compressor dehumidifiers work in cold rooms?
faqs.a: Standard models lose output and can ice up as rooms drop into the low 60s and below. Low-temp units with auto-defrost, like the AlorAir Sentinel HD55, work down to about 36°F.
